subject: Post-call: SLOs & graceful-degradation checklist — Redwood x AtlasPay
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Tanya Rios <tanya.rios@atlaspay.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — SLOs & graceful degradation (Redwood x AtlasPay)

Hi Tanya / Marco,

Thanks again for taking time today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to iterate. I tried to capture the pain points you raised, the way you currently run inference, and measurable success criteria. Please correct anything I missed.

Call summary (high level)
- Pain: recent multi-region incidents causing checkout latency spikes and partial auth failures.
- Business impact: estimated loss of completed transactions during incidents ~1.8% / week; increased support load for fraud/auth falls.
- Current stack: in-house model endpoints running on EC2 GPU instances (g4dn family), single-region primary with manual failover; primary model is "gpt-x-small" with an unpublished micro fallback that is currently cold. No standardized KV/prefix caching.
- Existing SLOs: internal target is 99.95% availability; no formal P95/P99 latency SLOs tracked across regions.

What success looks like (what you asked us to help prove)
- SLOs: P95 < 250ms for your 1k qps baseline; P99 within 400ms for auth-critical flows.
- Availability: automatic region failover to preserve auth/checkout during a zone or regional outage (target: 99.95% platform availability).
- Graceful degradation: deterministic fallback model with preserved output semantics for high-cardinality prompts; predictable cost/latency tradeoffs documented.
- Operational: reduced incident MTTR and a runbook for interim degraded modes (e.g., reduce context length, enforce light-weight fallback).

Short-term next steps (proposed)
1) I attached a one-page SLO checklist (redwood-slo-checklist.pdf) — please review and mark priority items.
2) Tech deep-dive with your infra/engine team + our solutions engineer (Aditya) — suggested 60-minute slot next week to go over topology and the incident timeline you mentioned.
3) Pilot: propose a 4-week dedicated-capacity pilot with a small canary region to validate warm fallback and prefix KV caching. We will provide a targeted runbook and cost estimate.
4) Compliance: you mentioned SOC 2 and evidence for data separation — Hannah will pull the attestation documents once we have NDA/contract alignment.

Attachments referenced: redwood-slo-checklist.pdf (one-pager), sample pilot timeline (inline).

Would love your confirmation on which of the following is highest priority: (A) reduce checkout latency tail, (B) implement automatic region failover, (C) shorten incident MTTR via warmed fallbacks.

Thanks,

— Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0122
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap — SLOs & graceful degradation (Redwood x AtlasPay)

Thanks Soojin — this is great, and captures our conversation. A couple of clarifications and notes from our side:

- Priority: (B) automatic region failover is primary — we can tolerate slightly higher latency during failover but cannot have auth/checkout failures. Secondary is (A) reduce tail latency.
- Incident history: attached is a compact timeline (incident-timeline.csv) for the last 6 months showing 3 region-level blips (Apr 18, May 3, Jun 11). The May 3 event caused a 2.2% revenue drop for a 3-hour window.
- Current failover: manual DNS swap + rebuild in another region — takes 30–90 minutes depending on warm cache. That’s the main gap.
- Compliance: SOC 2 is required for our procurement; please include your SOC 2 report and an outline for KMS/HSM options in the next packet.

Open question: can you share a ballpark monthly cost for a pilot (4 weeks) supporting our 1k baseline qps with a warmed fallback? We understand it will be a range but want to set internal expectations.

Happy to do the technical deep-dive next Tue 07/07 — mornings PT work best.

Thanks,
Tanya
Head of Platform, AtlasPay

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Tanya Rios <tanya.rios@atlaspay.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap — SLOs & graceful degradation (Redwood x AtlasPay)

Hi Tanya — quick technical follow-up and some concrete suggestions you can evaluate ahead of the deep-dive.

Technical observations from our side
- Warmed fallbacks: your current micro fallback is cold — that explains long failover times. We recommend a warmed fallback pool always available in a different AZ/region configured with sticky KV prefix warmers for auth prompt prefixes.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching for repeated auth prompts will reduce tail and P99 considerably for short-context requests. We can run a small pilot to show delta.
- Batching and concurrency: continuous batching tuned to your request size distribution will reduce per-token cost and smooth latency spikes.
- Quantization: model quantization (int8) for fallback models preserves semantics for auth checks while giving ~2–3x throughput improvement; primary can stay in higher precision.
- Routing/fallbacks: we propose policy-based routing: region-first, then warmed-fallback-model family (redwood-compact-v1) in a secondary region, then last-resort degraded-mode that truncates context and enforces a conservative response budget.

Pilot proposal (high level)
- Duration: 4 weeks (1 week prep + 2 weeks canary + 1 week scale/analysis)
- Scope: 1 primary region + 1 warm-fallback region, warmed pools (small), KV prefix cache enabled for auth flows, monitoring hooks for P95/P99, and an automatic fallback policy.
- Measurables: show P95/P99 deltas, cold-start latency distributions, MTTR to full traffic switch.

Estimated ballpark cost for 4-week pilot (very rough)
- Dedicated small pool + warm fallback + monitoring: $18k–$28k (depends on steady concurrency and storage for KV caches). We’ll provide a precise quote after topology review.

Attachments & resources
- I’m attaching a proposed architecture diagram (proposed-architecture.drawio) and a pilot checklist. Also listing a link to our pilot runbook.

Proposed next step: technical deep-dive Tue 07/07 10:00–11:00 PT (we’ll send calendar invite if that works).

— Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
